# Historical note: SN 1987A (not used for ms triangulation)

SN 1987A is the only CCSN with confirmed MeV neutrino detections
(Kamiokande-II, IMB, Baksan). It is **real** multimessenger history, but the
published absolute clocks are **not** synchronized at the light-travel (~ms)
level needed for DiffPointing:

| Detector | Published first-event UT | Clock caveat | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kamiokande-II | 1987-02-23 07:35:35 | ±60 s | Hirata et al., PRL 58, 1490 (1987) |
| IMB | 1987-02-23 07:35:41.374 | ±0.050 s | Bionta et al., PRL 58, 1494 (1987) |
| Baksan | 1987-02-23 07:36:11.818 | large asymmetric | Alekseev et al. / later compilations |

SN position (LMC / Sanduleak −69°202), J2000 approx. RA 05h35m28s,
Dec −69°16′12″ (~51.4 kpc) — see e.g. USNO / SN 1987A literature.

BREAKOUT therefore **does not** invent synchronized arrival times for a
1987A triangulation demo. For real-data localization validation we use the
IceCube historical alert catalog and IceCube-170922A / GCN notices instead.
SNEWS-style DiffPointing is exercised on modern multi-detector **simulated**
bursts (Scenario A) and on single-detector **real** IceCube pointing maps.
